factProposals.value: Relay has three outcomes for a dequeued job: processed, routed to the review queue (low confidence), or dead-lettered (failed). The review queue is its own Redis stream, separate from the DLQ.
The low-confidence threshold (0.5) is a placeholder defined once in confidence.ts; the real value is a product decision tied to the classification taxonomy (STORY-011).

decisions.statement: If the review queue can't be written to after capped retries, the job falls back to the DLQ tagged review_queue_unavailable instead of being dropped or processed.
decisions.rationale: the job has already been acked off the main stream, so failing to place it anywhere would lose it; the DLQ keeps it visible and triageable while still not resolving it.

decisions.statement: processJob refuses to resolve a low-confidence job on its own, in addition to the router sending it to review.
decisions.rationale: defense in depth for the 'low-confidence job is auto-resolved' failure path: any caller that bypasses the router still cannot resolve one, and the idempotency key stays unclaimed so it can be resolved after review.

decisions.statement: The existing end-to-end test that expected a low-confidence job to come back 'processed' was changed to expect needs_review.
decisions.rationale: that expectation encoded exactly the behavior REQ-010 forbids; keeping it would have locked in the bug.

limitations.statement: There is no reviewer workflow yet: entries wait in the review stream, but nothing lets a human approve, correct or reject them and resolve the job.
The MCP server's relay://jobs/needs-review resource still returns fixture data rather than reading the real review stream.
